description: Lamb Ouzi is a magnificent Middle Eastern feast featuring slow-roasted lamb, fragrant spiced rice, and a medley of toasted nuts. This impressive dish is perfect for celebrations, offering tender, falling-off-the-bone meat infused with aromatic spices. Prepare to delight your guests with this truly unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare and Marinate the Lamb
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine 1/4 cup olive oil, 2 tablespoons salt, 1 tablespoon black pepper, 3 tablespoons 7-spice blend, 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon, 1 teaspoon ground cardamom, 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves, minced garlic, and 1/4 cup lemon juice to form a paste. Score the lamb leg or shoulder deeply all over. Rub the spice paste generously into the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored areas. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and refrigerate to marinate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight.

instructions.title: Sear the Lamb and Begin Roasting
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Before placing the lamb in the oven, you can optionally sear it on all sides in a large oven-safe pot or pan over high heat until browned. This adds depth of flavor. Once seared or directly from marination, add 2 cups of lamb broth or water to the roasting pan. Cover the pan tightly with foil or a lid. Place in the preheated oven and slow roast for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until the lamb is fork-tender and easily pulls apart.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice Base
instructions.text: About 45 minutes before the lamb is done, drain the soaked basmati rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced yellow onion and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the diced carrots and cook for another 3 minutes. Stir in 1 teaspoon of 7-spice blend, 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Cook the Fragrant Rice
instructions.text: Add the drained basmati rice to the pot with the vegetables and spices. Stir well to coat the rice grains. Pour in 6 cups of lamb or chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, stir in the frozen peas, re-cover, and cook for another 5-10 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Toast the Garnish Nuts
instructions.text: While the rice is cooking, heat a small dry skillet over medium-low heat. Add the pine nuts and slivered almonds. Toast them gently, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them, as they can toast quickly. Remove from heat and set aside.

instructions.title: Assemble and Serve the Lamb Ouzi
instructions.text: Carefully remove the slow-roasted lamb from the oven. Let it rest for 15-20 minutes, covered, before shredding the meat off the bone using two forks. Fluff the cooked Ouzi rice with a fork. On a large serving platter, spread the fragrant Ouzi rice. Arrange the shredded lamb generously over the rice. Garnish with the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and freshly chopped parsley. Serve immediately and enjoy this magnificent Middle Eastern feast.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your 7-spice blend is fresh; consider grinding your own spices for a more intense aroma. Do not rush the slow roasting process for the lamb, as patience yields the most tender, fall-off-the-bone results.

If a whole lamb leg is too much, this recipe works beautifully with a lamb shoulder or even large lamb shanks. You can also substitute basmati rice with long-grain rice, adjusting cooking time and liquid as needed.

Leftover Lamb Ouzi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in the microwave or oven, adding a splash of broth to the rice to maintain moisture. It also freezes well for up to 2 months.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East with a dish that embodies celebration, warmth, and incredible flavor: Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted. More than just a meal, Ouzi is an experience – a magnificent centerpiece traditionally reserved for special occasions, family gatherings, and festive feasts. Imagine succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb, infused with aromatic spices, nestled atop a bed of fragrant, spiced basmati rice, adorned with toasted nuts. This isn't just a dinner; it's a statement, a testament to the rich culinary heritage of the region. Preparing a whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi might seem daunting, but with this comprehensive guide, you'll discover that patience and passion are the main ingredients for an unforgettable feast. Get ready to impress your guests and delight your senses with this truly spectacular Middle Eastern dinner recipe.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled Ghuzi or Ouze, is a revered dish across the Middle East, particularly popular in countries like Iraq, Syria, Jordan, and the Gulf States. At its core, Ouzi is a combination of slow-cooked, tender lamb and highly seasoned rice, often served on a grand platter, making it a visual and gastronomic showstopper. While some variations might feature smaller cuts of lamb or even chicken, the most impressive and traditional rendition involves a whole lamb, or at least a substantial cut like a leg or shoulder, slow roasted until it's incredibly tender.

The magic of this dish lies in its layered flavors. The lamb is typically marinated in a blend of spices that often includes cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, black pepper, and turmeric, allowing these aromatics to penetrate deep into the meat during the long, slow roasting process. The accompanying rice is equally flavorful, cooked with lamb stock, more spices, and often enriched with vegetables like peas and carrots, and studded with toasted nuts such as almonds, pine nuts, or cashews. The result is a harmonious blend of savory, earthy, and fragrant notes that define Middle Eastern cuisine. This Lamb Ouzi recipe is a true expression of hospitality and generosity.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Crafting the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires quality ingredients and a thoughtful approach to seasoning. Here’s what you’ll need for a magnificent whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi (using a substantial cut like a large leg or shoulder, typically 5-7 lbs, for home preparation):

**For the Lamb:**
*   1 large lamb leg or shoulder (approx. 5-7 lbs), bone-in preferred
*   Marinade:
    *   1/4 cup olive oil
    *   4-6 cloves garlic, minced
    *   2 tbsp ground cumin
    *   2 tbsp ground coriander
    *   1 tbsp ground cinnamon
    *   1 tbsp ground cardamom
    *   1 tsp ground cloves
    *   1 tsp ground nutmeg
    *   1 tsp black pepper
    *   1 tbsp salt (or to taste)
    *   Juice of 1 lemon
    *   1/4 cup plain yogurt (optional, for tenderizing)
*   2 large onions, quartered
*   4-6 cups lamb or beef broth (for basting and roasting)

**For the Spiced Rice (Ouzi Rice):**
*   3 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   1/4 cup olive oil or ghee
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   2 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 tbsp ground cinnamon
*   1 tsp ground cardamom
*   1/2 tsp ground cloves
*   1/2 tsp ground nutmeg
*   1/2 tsp black pepper
*   1 tsp salt (or to taste)
*   5-6 cups lamb or chicken broth
*   1 cup frozen peas (optional)
*   1/2 cup shredded carrots (optional)

**For Garnish:**
*   1/2 cup almonds, slivered or whole, toasted
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1/4 cup fresh parsley, chopped
*   Lemon wedges

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Lamb Ouzi

This detailed Lamb Ouzi recipe will guide you through each stage, ensuring a flavorful and tender result.

**1. Prepare and Marinate the Lamb (Overnight Recommended):**
*   Pat the lamb leg or shoulder dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the surface of the lamb deeply in a diamond pattern, being careful not to cut through to the bone. This helps the marinade penetrate.
*   In a bowl, combine all the marinade ingredients (olive oil, garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, black pepper, salt, lemon juice, and optional yogurt). Mix well.
*   Rub the marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored crevices. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover tightly, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.

**2. Slow Roast the Lamb:**
*   Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C).
*   Remove the lamb from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature for about an hour.
*   Place the quartered onions around the lamb in the roasting pan. Pour 2 cups of lamb or beef broth into the bottom of the pan.
*   Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil or a lid. This traps the moisture and ensures the lamb steams and tenderizes.
*   Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The cooking time will vary depending on the size and cut of lamb. Every hour or so, baste the lamb with the pan juices, adding more broth if the pan seems dry.
*   For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and develop a crust. You can also increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) for the final browning if desired.
*   Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving or shredding. This is crucial for juicy lamb. Reserve the pan juices.

**3. Prepare the Spiced Rice (Ouzi Rice):**
*   While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. Heat olive oil or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
*   Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
*   Stir in the ground cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, black pepper, and salt. Cook for 1 minute, allowing the spices to bloom.
*   Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot and stir to coat every grain with the spiced oil. Cook for 2-3 minutes, lightly toasting the rice.
*   Pour in the lamb or chicken broth. If using, add the frozen peas and shredded carrots. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
*   Once cooked, remove from heat and let it sit, covered, for another 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork.

**4. Toast the Nuts and Garnish:**
*   In a dry skillet over medium-low heat, toast the slivered almonds and pine nuts separately until golden brown and fragrant. Watch them carefully as they can burn quickly.

**5. Assemble and Serve:**
*   On a large serving platter, spread the spiced Ouzi rice evenly.
*   Gently place the whole slow roasted lamb on top of the rice. You can shred some of the lamb and mix it into the rice for a more integrated presentation.
*   Generously sprinkle the toasted almonds, pine nuts, and chopped fresh parsley over the lamb and rice.
*   Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side. This Lamb Ouzi recipe is best enjoyed fresh!

## Expert Tips for Perfect Lamb Ouzi

Achieving the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires attention to detail. Here are some expert tips to elevate your dish:

*   **Quality Lamb:** Start with good quality lamb. A bone-in leg or shoulder provides more flavor and stays moister during the long cooking process.
*   **Marinade Time is Key:** Don't skimp on the marinating time. Overnight is ideal to allow the spices to truly penetrate the meat, resulting in a deeply flavorful lamb.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way:** The "slow roasted" part of this Lamb Ouzi recipe is non-negotiable. Cooking at a low temperature for several hours breaks down the tough fibers in the lamb, yielding incredibly tender, melt-in-your-mouth meat.
*   **Rest the Lamb:** Always rest the lamb after roasting. This allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring it remains moist and flavorful when carved.
*   **Don't Overcook the Rice:** Basmati rice cooks quickly. Follow the instructions precisely and avoid lifting the lid during cooking to ensure perfectly fluffy, separate grains.
*   **Toast Nuts Separately:** Toasting different nuts separately allows you to achieve optimal browning for each, as they cook at different rates. This enhances their flavor and crunch.
*   **Use Lamb Broth:** Whenever possible, use lamb broth for both the roasting process and the rice. It amplifies the lamb flavor significantly. If unavailable, good quality beef or chicken broth will suffice.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but traditional accompaniments further enhance the dining experience.

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple plain yogurt, perhaps mixed with a little minced garlic and dried mint, offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the lamb.
*   **Fresh Salads:** Light, crisp Middle Eastern salads like Fattoush (mixed greens with toasted pita bread, sumac, and a lemon-sumac dressing) or Tabbouleh (finely chopped parsley, tomatoes, mint, bulgur, and lemon dressing) provide freshness and acidity.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips, cucumbers, or olives) add a tangy crunch that cuts through the richness.
*   **Warm Bread:** Freshly baked pita bread or flatbread is perfect for scooping up any extra rice or lamb.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always serve extra lemon wedges. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice brightens the entire dish.

Present your Lamb Ouzi on a large, ornate platter, making it the undeniable centerpiece of your table. The visual appeal is almost as important as the taste for such a grand dish.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While the traditional Lamb Ouzi recipe is glorious, there's room for creativity and adaptation:

*   **Lamb Cut Variations:** If a whole leg or shoulder is too much, you can use smaller cuts like lamb shanks or even a boneless lamb roast. Adjust cooking times accordingly. For a quicker Ouzi, some recipes call for lamb cubes stewed until tender.
*   **Meat Alternatives:** While lamb is classic, a whole slow roasted chicken or even beef roast can be prepared with similar spices and served over the Ouzi rice for a different flavor profile.
*   **Rice Additions:** Beyond peas and carrots, you can incorporate other vegetables into the rice, such as bell peppers, chickpeas, or even dried fruits like raisins or currants for a touch of sweetness.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to adjust the spice levels to your preference. If you enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of cayenne pepper or chili flakes can be added to the lamb marinade or rice.
*   **Nut Variations:** Experiment with different nuts for garnish. Toasted walnuts or pistachios can also add a delightful texture and flavor.
*   **Smoked Flavor:** For an authentic touch, some traditional Ouzi recipes involve a brief smoking process for the lamb after roasting, using charcoal and oil to impart a smoky aroma. This can be replicated at home with a small piece of charcoal in a foil cup placed within the roasting pan, briefly covered.

Mastering the whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi is a rewarding culinary achievement that brings the rich flavors and festive spirit of Middle Eastern cuisine to your home. This comprehensive Lamb Ouzi recipe will guide you to a spectacular dish that will be remembered long after the last bite. It’s more than just a meal; it’s an experience, a celebration of flavor, and a testament to the joys of slow cooking. So gather your ingredients, set aside the time, and prepare to create a truly magnificent Middle Eastern feast.
